Alex — thanks for the sample and context. I pulled a quick pass on hit-rate expectations and how that maps to effective $/1M tokens. Below are pragmatic assumptions we use when modeling pricing for customers with similar usage.

Definitions / cache types
- Prefix cache: caches model outputs for identical prompt prefixes (highly effective when system prompts are common and user prompts vary).
- Session cache (KV cache): re-uses key/value KV cache across turns within the same session to avoid re-computing earlier tokens.

Assumptions (example):
- Baseline raw cost (no cache) = $3,500 / 1M raw tokens (typical for the model + infra profile we discussed).
- Effective billable tokens = raw tokens * (1 - hit_rate).

Example scenarios (illustrative):
- Low cache effectiveness (20% hit rate): billable = 0.80 * tokens => effective cost = $2,800 / 1M tokens
- Mid cache effectiveness (40% hit rate): billable = 0.60 * tokens => effective cost = $2,100 / 1M tokens
- High cache effectiveness (60% hit rate): billable = 0.40 * tokens => effective cost = $1,400 / 1M tokens

Notes on hit-rate drivers for Acme (from your sample):
- System prefixes: your dataset shows ~65% of sessions include the same 2–3 system prompts (good candidate for prefix caching).
- Repeat user queries: medium — ~18% exact repeats in 2-week sample.
- Multi-turn sessions: average 4 turns; session KV cache yields savings but less than prefix cache for your workload.

Realistic expected hit-rate for initial production: 30–45% with prefix + session caching enabled. That implies an effective cost of roughly $1,925–2,450 / 1M tokens using the $3,500 baseline.

Mapping to your budget target ($900–1,200): to reach that level we'd need either: 
1) Much higher hit rates (~70–75%) OR
2) A different model/infra profile (cheaper baseline) or negotiated committed pricing (reserved capacity) that lowers the baseline from $3,500 to ~$1,000–1,500 / 1M raw tokens.

Suggested next steps:
- Redwood does a short technical deep-dive (30–45m) to confirm cacheable prefixes and session patterns — we can run a small offline simulation against your sample to produce a more precise hit-rate estimate.
- Based on that sim + projected volumes, we will produce 3 pricing scenarios (on-demand, committed reserved, and committed + caching-optimized) with effective $/1M tokens and monthly spend estimates.

I can run the sim early next week if you share a full month sample (or we can use the attached 2-week extract with a scale-up multiplier). I’ll drop the sim results into the RIFP-pricing-model.xlsx and link it back to the deal.

— Marcus
